artifacts.summary: Research on the missing bounded local-detached-command waiter idiom: confirms the dead-end pointer in external-process-wait.md, generalizes lake-build-guard.sh's existing kill -0 idiom, sharpens writer-liveness to PID-only (never process-name matching), and recommends four mandatory properties plus a long-builds.md pointer wired per the single-statement-plus-pointer convention.

memory_candidates.content: In this source store, a new core context pattern file's forward-reference may already exist in a sibling file before the new file is written (e.g. external-process-wait.md named bounded-build-waiter.md in its Related/cross-reference sections before that file existed). When researching a 'write new pattern file' task, grep existing sibling pattern files for a premature pointer to the target filename first -- it often pre-confirms the expected structure, properties, and audience without further investigation.

Process-liveness polling in this codebase must key on a captured PID (pid=$!; kill -0 "$pid") and never on process-name/argv matching (ps aux | grep, pgrep -f) -- a polling shell whose own argv contains the search pattern (e.g. because it launched the very command it is polling for, or because the pattern names the polling script itself) self-matches and the loop never terminates. This bug class recurred independently in lake-build-guard.sh's own documented pitfall, a BimodalLogic reaper self-kill, and a Logos/Verification 5x hang on `ps aux | grep -q "[b]ash script.sh"` where the bracket trick failed to protect against the LAUNCHING shell's own argv.
